items.summary: China's National Development and Reform Commission blocked SoftBank's US$5.4 billion acquisition of engineering group ABB's robotics division, the Swiss firm said on Nov 5. This follows Meta being ordered to unwind its deal with Manus earlier in 2026. The NDRC cited concerns over robotics data flowing overseas for AI training. ABB shares fell 1.1%, while SoftBank shares dropped about 5% before and 6.8% at close.
items.title: China Rejects SoftBank Bid for ABB Robotics Unit

items.summary: Three Orchard Central tenants told by landlord Far East Organization to vacate levels 5 to 12 by end-November have moved to JustCo Place at 160 Orchard Road. Evolve MMA, Helen's and K. STAR Karaoke will occupy the site; Evolve MMA takes a 10,000 sq ft flagship there. Retailers are expected to open progressively from December, with co-living space due in 2027. JustCo Holdings said it has secured retail leasing commitment for 80% of its retail space.
items.title: Orchard Central tenants relocate across road to JustCo Place

items.summary: OpenAI shipped image models Flare and Sunburst across ChatGPT, Codex and the API. The release adds animated GIF output, SVG export, markup-guided edits and a complexity parameter with no extra fee. OpenAI states images generate about 50% faster than before, with Flare returning an image in as little as 6 seconds at low quality. Weekly generation rose from more than 3B to more than 4B across ChatGPT and the API, averaging over 500M per day. Token pricing is $30 per million output tokens; OpenAI notes no benchmark scores or per-image cost table for 2.6.
items.title: OpenAI Ships Images 2.6 With GIF and SVG Support

items.summary: Protesters across Europe are planning two days of action against datacentres this week with demonstrations taking place in 15 countries. More than 100 groups are joining together for the “Stop Dirty Data Centres” events on Friday and Saturday, calling for a moratorium on large projects citing environmental costs that “we can no longer afford”. Owen Espley, campaign coordinator, said communities across Europe are rising up to demand politicians impose moratoria. Organisers expect attendance ranging from a handful at some gatherings to several hundred at larger ones such as in Brick Lane and Dublin. Groups backing the protests include Friends of the Earth, Greenpeace and Foxglove.
items.title: European Activists Plan Two-Day Datacentre Protests Across 15 Countries

items.summary: Bitdefender disclosed a vulnerability dubbed 'GhostMap' that lets an app with no permissions trigger a persistent boot loop on Android devices. The flaw stems from two libraries interpreting ZIP compression differently, causing malformed APKs to bypass size checks and crash the affected process when reading unallocated memory. Researchers demonstrated it using a Pixel 10 running Android 17. Bitdefender reported the issue to Google in August but was classified 'not reproducible.' Remediation options include factory reset or deleting the file via ADB.
items.title: Bitdefender Discloses Android GhostMap Flaw Causing Boot Loops

items.summary: A ferocious storm last weekend inundated communities across the Southwest, killing at least four people after Clovis, New Mexico received 28.84 inches of rain versus a historical average of just 3.3 inches in September 20. Russ Schumacher of the Colorado Climate Center called the El Niño connection clear and said warmer Pacific waters are priming much of the southern United States for increased winter precipitation, per NOAA's outlook. Michael A. Crimmins of the University of Arizona noted such an event could occur without El Niño but would be far less likely. Any added rainfall might ease drought strain on Lake Powell and Lake Mead, though Schumacher said it cannot reverse their decline.
items.title: El Niño storms flood Southwest and may bring wetter winter

items.summary: Researchers at South Korea's Dongguk University built an anode-free all-solid-state battery prototype that delivered a volumetric energy density of 235.13 Wh/L, the researchers reported. The design uses an ultrathin tin/carbon interlayer on a copper current collector to guide lithium deposition and includes prelithiation to offset early losses. Lead author Hyun-Suk Kim said the approach could support thin-film batteries for wearable electronics and scalable industrial power.
items.title: Korean Researchers Prototype High-Density All-Solid-State Battery

items.summary: Nippon Steel Kowa Real Estate, Sumitomo Life Insurance and Obayashi Corp. are implementing a green hydrogen project at Shinagawa Intercity in Tokyo’s Minato ward. It is the first to receive funding under the Tokyo Metropolitan Government’s support program for practical green hydrogen production. Rooftop solar panels generate electricity used to produce hydrogen via electrolysis, which is stored and converted back into power through fuel cells. The companies have not disclosed installed capacities or storage volumes. Separately, they introduced an off-site physical corporate PPA expected to supply about 3 GWh of renewable electricity annually with around 1,200 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions reduction per year.
items.title: Tokyo Companies Test Solar-Powered Hydrogen at Office Complex

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, the first increase since February 2023, while injecting ₹2.5 lakh crore liquidity into banks. Lending expert Joydeep Gupta explained that higher rates may raise home and personal loan costs over roughly three months for floating-rate borrowers, though new lending need not become harder; attention turns to the December MPC meeting on 2-4 December 2026.
items.title: RBI Raises Repo Rate While Injecting Liquidity

items.summary: Bharti Airtel chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal plans a global satellite network to reduce reliance on the US and China, per Bloomberg. His Eutelsat OneWeb faces SpaceX's Starlink, which has over 10,000 satellites versus OneWeb's roughly 650.
items.title: Sunil Bharti Mittal Prepares Starlink Rival OneWeb Satellite Network

items.summary: According to a person familiar with the matter, Microsoft will not exercise an option that would have more than doubled its existing agreement with AI cloud provider Nscale for computing power at a Texas data center. The Financial Times first reported the news; a potential extension would have been worth tens of billions of dollars for Nscale. Microsoft and Nscale did not respond to comment requests.
items.title: Microsoft declines option to expand Nscale Texas data center deal

items.summary: Analysts expect the Bank of England to raise rates at its meeting, with Deutsche Bank predicting a split vote in favour of the move. Meanwhile, the FTSE 100 hit a three-month high as markets reacted positively.
items.title: Bank of England Rate Hike and FTSE Record High

items.summary: A second buyer, Xyra Group, has made a rescue bid for discount retailer Poundland as it faces collapse with thousands of jobs at risk. London-based Xyra offered to immediately repay £12.5m of the firm's £30m outstanding loan, though doubts remain over its credibility and whether buyers meet Gordon Brothers' tests. US owners Gordon Brothers rejected an earlier Irish bid and urged protection of staff during talks led by Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds.
items.title: Xyra Group Rescues Poundland Amid Collapse Fears

items.summary: The Democrats' sweep in the US midterm elections, which gave them control of the Senate and House, is being read as a win for the global renewable energy industry. Across financial centres worldwide, developers saw their market value climb; Ørsted jumped almost 10% within hours before closing almost 5% higher, while Portugal's EDP Renewables and France's Engie rose more than 3%, Germany's RWE about 1%. The rally comes after the Danish firm lost more than 70% of its market value since Trump returned to office in 2025. Analysts say the shift may reduce regulatory risk, protect solar and wind tax credits, and ease financing for new projects. Brenda Shaffer called it an energy election; Jason Grumet said affordable power is now a priority.
items.title: Midterm victory lifts renewable energy stocks after Trump hostility

items.summary: Brent crude futures edged up 78 cents, or 0.8 per cent, to $95.40 a barrel as investors weighed the future of the US-Israeli war with Iran following Republican midterm losses this week. UBS's Giovanni Staunovo said prices showed modest recovery while the Middle East situation stays unresolved. Eurasia Group cut its estimate for renewed strikes on Iran to 60 per cent, though it raised odds of a continued standoff and warned volatility could push Brent toward $110 to $125.
items.title: Brent crude rises on Iran war uncertainty after US midterms

items.summary: A speaker argues that recent American elections produced resoundingly moderate outcomes, repudiating both Trump and the extreme Democratic left, while trends in teen mental health are positive. These developments occur as social media usage continues unabated and short video rises further. The speaker concludes these results indicate standard anti-social media polemics are radically incomplete and currently failing in their predictions, though neither trend is guaranteed to continue.
items.title: Moderate election results and rising teen wellbeing challenge social media critiques

items.summary: The pound rose to its highest level since the June 2016 referendum, according to Bank of England figures. A basket measure against 18 currencies reached an index value of 86.4, where 100 equals 2005 levels. The rise follows political stability and growth ahead of a widely expected interest rate increase on Thursday. Economist Jim O'Neill said people were underestimating the UK's improving momentum.
items.title: Sterling Reaches Highest Level Since Brexit Referendum Amid Expected Rate Rise

items.summary: Google, with the National Police Agency (NPA), said it disabled a backdoor that turned about 1.3 million Videostrong-manufactured Android TV boxes into malware-infected residential proxies. The NPA linked unauthorized bank transfers to these proxies in roughly 1,918 cases worth around ¥2.89 billion ($18.3 million) in 2024.
items.title: Google and Japan's police shut down Chinese backdoor in internet devices

items.summary: The 140th Canton Fair in Guangzhou is closing on November 4 after drawing 32,000 exhibitors. Organizers say the expo centered on robots, AI and green technology: 64% of exhibitors integrated industrial internet and AI into R&D, while new products made up a record 23.2% of exhibits. Customs data shows China's imports and exports of industrial robots, electronic components, computer parts and electrical equipment surged 58.9% year on year, topping 10 trillion yuan ($1.49 trillion) in the first three quarters of 2026. Officials frame the fair as evidence that Chinese trade is running on a brand-new model built around higher-value products and more comprehensive services.
items.title: Canton Fair Marks China's Shift Toward High-Value Trade

items.summary: A webpage promotes a 90-second video showing the construction of Adora Flora City, described as China's second domestically built large cruise ship. After four years of building, it is scheduled to be officially delivered on Nov. 6 in Shanghai and will begin commercial voyages on Nov. 22, focusing on southern China and Southeast Asia. The vessel has 2,130 cabins and can hold up to 5,232 passengers at full capacity.
items.title: China's Second Domestically Built Large Cruise Ship Set for Delivery

items.summary: A group of military attachés visited a museum in Zunyi, Guizhou Province, to practice calligraphy while learning about the history of the Long March. The foreign guests wrote "Loushan Pass" on Wednesday at a museum displaying Mao Zedong's poems. Loushan Pass was where the Red Army gained its first major victory since the beginning of the Long March in 1935.
items.title: Military Attachés Study Calligraphy and Long March History in Zunyi

items.summary: The 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Foreign Ministers' Meeting was held Wednesday in Beijing. The six member countries reviewed a decade of cooperation and pledged closer ties, with new commitments in areas such as disaster prevention and artificial intelligence.
items.title: Six Nations Pledge Closer Ties at Lancang-Mekong Meeting in Beijing

items.summary: A Beihang University team is designing a conceptual road on the moon, made from crushed stone excavated in situ or sintered there. Professor Li Feng told CGTN that modern roads began as gravel surfaces, so the lunar version could follow suit. The Qinzhidao concept honors an ancient Chinese highway over 2,200 years old. Published January 2026 in the China Journal of Highway and Transport.
items.title: Beihang University Team Designs Concept for China's First Lunar Road

items.summary: The French prime minister's office said an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome was diverted to a military base in Évreux after a bomb alert. Flightradar24 reported no aircraft departed Fiumicino Airport in the past 30 minutes and described the plane veering toward France before circling without landing. The incident followed seven European flights searched or diverted two days earlier.
items.title: Aer Lingus Flight Diverted After Bomb Threat in France

items.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage appointed Angus MacIntyre, an RAF wing commander with a 40-year career, as its shadow armed forces minister. In interviews Michel Barnier said the UK could rejoin the single market without joining the euro but free movement would remain non-negotiable.
items.title: UK can avoid euro but must accept free movement to rejoin EU, says former top Brexit negotiator – UK politics live

items.summary: A plane flying from Dublin to Rome was rerouted to Evreux airbase in France on Thursday (Nov 5) after a bomb threat, the French government said. Quoting Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's office, Reuters reported the Airbus A320 diversion. Flight-tracking site Flightradar24 noted an Aer Lingus aircraft declared an emergency and circled near Paris. The incident followed about 10 European flights targeted by bomb threats on Tuesday.
items.title: Dublin-Rome Flight Diverted After Bomb Threat, France Says

items.summary: Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in Brisbane after refusing to serve ham and pineapple pizza, which he called an insult to his culture. Australia's Fair Work Commission ruled against him on a late filing. Managing director Elliot Ingram said there was more to the case than toppings.
items.title: Italian Chef Fired Over Pineapple Pizza Refusal Loses Claim

items.summary: An Airbus A320 flying from Dublin to Rome was diverted to Evreux airfield west of Paris after a bomb threat, according to the office of French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu. Tracking websites showed it deviating sharply near Paris before landing safely. The incident follows hoax threats earlier this week that caused diversions and security mobilizations across several European airlines.
items.title: Aer Lingus flight diverted amid bomb threat

items.summary: An article argues that team sports like American football rely heavily on tactical innovation, using the Chicago Bears' Monday Night Football win over Seattle as an example. Head coach Ben Johnson deployed formations and plays that disrupted the Seahawks' defense. The piece contrasts this with individual sports, where such coordinated scheming is less central.
items.title: Sumo's peak optimization mirrors football's technical innovation

items.summary: An Airbus A320 flying from Dublin to Rome was diverted Thursday to France's Evreux airbase after a bomb threat, the French prime minister's office said. It is part of recent threats against European flights; some 10 were targeted Tuesday, closing Warsaw airport briefly and scrambling planes in Rome. No one was injured.
items.title: Bomb Threat Diverts Dublin-Rome Flight to French Base

items.summary: Bob Dylan visited Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican Wednesday during a break between concert dates in Italy, an encounter described by the Vatican as brief. The pope gave Dylan a rosary and received his autobiography Chronicles: Volume One. Spadaro said Dylan wanted to speak privately with Leo for a few minutes.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Welcomes Bob Dylan at Vatican

items.summary: France is bracing for a nationwide strike as hundreds of thousands of protestors are expected on Thursday, involving trade unions, the yellow vest movement, students and workers across sectors. The mobilisation follows lawmakers rejecting the first part of the 2027 budget bill in unified consensus. The government's original proposal will now go before the Senate, with a vote scheduled for 9 December. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez announced more than 70,000 law enforcement officers would be deployed to ensure demonstrations occur peacefully and without incidents. Trade unions condemned what they described as excessive policing amid ongoing debt and deficit concerns ahead of April elections.
items.title: France Prepares for Nationwide Strike Over Austerity Budget

items.summary: An Airbus airliner flying from Dublin to Rome was rerouted Thursday and escorted by military aircraft after a suspected bomb threat, French authorities said. The plane reached the Evreux airfield west of Paris while France's air force responded quickly. Separately, Bulgaria reported three Ryanair flights faced threats, with one diverted to Plovdiv. About 10 European flights were targeted Tuesday; the UK called them malicious hoax threats.
items.title: Airbus Flight Diverted After Bomb Alert

items.summary: The Queensland Police Union is urging mandatory minimum sentencing for serious assaults on police after an officer was allegedly attacked in Mount Isa, leaving him with a cut jaw. The union president said prison should be the only option. A Griffith University law lecturer argued harsher penalties would not deter offenders and could worsen court efficiency. Sentencing data shows such matters rose from 220 to 360 between financial years ending October 2019 and October 2025, with 48 per cent resulting in imprisonment and 20 per cent wholly suspended.
items.title: Queensland Police Union Pushes Mandatory Sentences After Mount Isa Assault

items.summary: A woman, whose identity was suppressed by Magistrate Clare Stanyer citing an ongoing matter, appeared at the Perth Magistrates Court accused of aggravated stalking with intent to intimidate and demanding property by written threats against WA Greens senator Jordon Steele-John. She is 40 years old and granted bail not contacting him. The allegations relate to workplace misconduct reports; Senator Steele-John denies them, while an external investigation runs.
items.title: Woman Charged With Stalking WA Greens Senator Appears in Court

items.summary: China's Macao Special Administrative Region has ranked first for consecutive years in the China Tourism Academy's ranking for Chinese outbound tourist satisfaction. The article frames green tourism as central to upgrading urban governance and sustainable development rather than mere sightseeing. Three experts weigh in: Wong Seng Fat of the Smart City Alliance Association describes it as an all-for-one model centered on ecological priority, cultural continuity, low-carbon emissions reduction and sustainable operations; Li Xi of City University of Macau cites three dimensions—strategic positioning, national dual-carbon alignment and community operating efficiency; Cui Wenjing notes governance is expanding from individual measures to destination-level management. Achievements include green hotel awards and wetland conservation, though bottlenecks such as limited resources, weak public awareness and incomplete standards remain.
items.title: Macao Leads China in Tourist Satisfaction, Pushes Green Tourism Transition

items.summary: After the Democrats captured both chambers of Congress, analysts weighed what it means for US economic policy while President Donald Trump keeps two years left in office. Markets rebounded after an initial dip as investors took heart from the Democratic victory. Stephen Brown of Capital Economics said the gains do not change much near-term outlook because the party lacks a filibuster-proof Senate majority and Trump holds veto power, which he may use to block legislation. Jacob Funk Kirkegaard warned of two years of gridlock but noted local opposition could still hinder data-center construction and weigh on big-tech valuations. Polling from Pew Research Center found 56% view Trump's tariff policies as mostly negative versus only 20% positive, a sentiment that helped Democrats win in export-heavy states.
items.title: Democrats' midterm win and its uncertain impact on Trump's economic agenda

items.summary: A passenger plane traveling from Dublin, Ireland, to Rome, Italy, was diverted to Evreux Air Base in Normandy after a bomb threat on board. The French prime minister's office told broadcaster BFMTV Thursday that the situation was being monitored in real time by its office. Flight-tracking website Flightradar24 reported the Aer Lingus A320 turning back over southern Paris before heading toward the air base.
items.title: Passenger Plane Diverted After Bomb Threat Reported Onboard

items.summary: Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense issued two brief 'potential danger' warnings for Sharurah governorate in the southwestern Najran region on Thursday via X and its National Early Warning Platform for Emergencies. Minutes later it announced the danger had passed without clarifying its nature or causes, urging residents to keep following instructions and avoid gathering or photographing. The alerts came amid continued Houthi missile and drone attacks; Saudi Arabia has led a coalition against Yemen's Houthis since March 2015 over territory held by them since September 2014.
items.title: Saudi Civil Defense Issues Two Warnings, Then Says Danger Passed

items.summary: Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono expressed “immense pain” after Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died the day following a collision between them in a second-division match on Monday. In a club statement released Wednesday, November 4, Owono called it “the most difficult days” of his life and said he faced questions with respect. Spanish media report he could face suspension or court action for negligent homicide. Tenerife declared six days of mourning; matches were postponed across Spain and Europe, with a funeral set in Navahermosa on Saturday, November 7.
items.title: Owono Mourns De Miguel as Tenerife Declares Mourning

items.summary: Kamal Al-Dabary, a 60-year-old former engineering student displaced from al-Mawasi near Khan Yunis, has built homemade wind turbines using scooter motors and salvaged components to generate power. The devices store energy in batteries and provide limited electricity for phones, lights, fans and razors. With solar panels costing nearly $5,000 and Gaza's infrastructure damaged, the invention offers an affordable alternative.
items.title: Displaced Palestinian builds wind turbines for electricity in Gaza

items.summary: Following Democrats' midterm election gains, analysts outline how the party might constrain President Donald Trump's war against Iran. Legislation faces limits: concurrent resolutions are non-binding and binding laws could be vetoed without a two-thirds majority. Investigations into the conflict would be lengthy, though impeachment of figures like Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth remains possible but unlikely to succeed. The most immediate tool is Congress's power of the purse under Article I, Section 9 of the US Constitution, which requires funding approval for new military spending. However, this could block all military paychecks and risk political backlash, as seen in a similar 2007 attempt over Iraq that President George W. Bush vetoed. Trump acknowledged the war's role in Republican losses but vowed to continue it if needed to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons.
items.title: Democrats Explore Funding Cuts to End Trump's Iran War

items.summary: In today's session, Ashok Leyland shares rose as much as 12% to Rs 172 on the BSE, while Tata Motors jumped 9% to Rs 440. The rally followed a sharp fall in crude oil prices and buoyant market sentiment after Democrats gained ground in US midterm elections. Analysts expect the bullish trend to continue amid easing global cues, though the article carries investment disclaimers from author Veer Sharma.
items.title: Tata Motors and Ashok Leyland Shares Surge on Crude Oil Drop

items.summary: Google announced it will switch off its Gemini and Search AI features by default on K-12 student accounts worldwide, beginning in the United States, with no date set. The move follows criticism over pushing artificial intelligence into classrooms while schools debate usage. Google framed the change as giving schools more choice, though New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused it of using monopoly power to force AI into public education.
items.title: Google Turns Off AI Tools for School Children By Default

items.summary: Elon Musk spent nearly half a billion dollars on the US midterm elections, but his companies fell after Democrats took both chambers of Congress. In premarket trading, shares of Musk-owned companies came under pressure, with SpaceX falling 3.8% in premarket trading and Tesla slipping 3.6%, as they underperformed the broader market even while equities rallied. The S&P 500 jumped 1.6%. An analysis by The New York Times suggests that Musk contributed $474 million to Republican candidates during the 2026 midterms, including almost $224 million in Texas alone, making him the biggest donor of the election by a considerable margin. Analysts and experts expect greater scrutiny of data-centre projects as Democrats control Congress.
items.title: Musk's Midterm Spending Backfires as Tesla and SpaceX Stocks Fall

items.summary: A Rohini-based Delhi company, which posts as Financersaab (@financersaab2.0), gave its employees iPhone 16 handsets instead of traditional sweets this Diwali and posted a short video on Instagram that went viral. Viewers praised the gesture while joking about job openings. The clip has not been independently verified beyond the company's own post, and the firm did not disclose how many staff received phones or the cost.
items.title: Delhi Firm Gifts iPhone 16 To Staff For Diwali, Internet Asks 'Any Vacancies?'

items.summary: The Centre told the Supreme Court on Thursday that it is contemplating constituting a committee to revisit the University Grants Commission's notified rules, which were introduced to prevent caste discrimination in educational institutions. The statement was conveyed through Bar and Bench, reported by digital journalist Rohitashwa Ranjan of The Times of India.
items.title: Centre tells Supreme Court it is considering a committee on UGC equity rules

items.summary: Crude futures slipped below $95, with WTI falling under $87 on Thursday morning. The decline lifted sentiment toward companies using oil as a raw material and airlines facing elevated fuel costs. IndiGo shares surged 7% to Rs 5,489 apiece; SpiceJet jumped around 5%. Asian Paints rallied nearly 7%, while Indigo Paints and Berger Paints rose up to 5%. MRF gained more than 4%, Apollo Tyres and Balkrishna Industries jumped over 8%, and oil marketing companies including HPCL, BPCL and IOC rose up to 7%. Analyst June Goh of Sparta Commodities said markets are pricing in a higher likelihood the war will end. Sunny Agrawal of SBI Securities noted that if crude stays below $90-100 per barrel, inflationary pressures could ease for India's economy and equity markets.
items.title: Indian crude-sensitive stocks rally as oil prices fall

items.summary: The Election Commission announced a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in six states and Union territories, including Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim. It directed the chief secretaries to provide adequate manpower so that final rolls are completed by January 21.
items.title: Election Commission Orders Electoral Roll Revision Across Six States and Union Territories

items.summary: A study published in Proceedings of the Zoological Society documents the Rabha community's traditional consumption of the Indian black earth tiger spider (Lyrognathus crotalus), collected from sal forests across western Assam. Researchers Jyotiprakash Boro, Kuldeep Bora, Chandramita Boro and Samir Terdalkar conducted fieldwork between April and June 2025, interviewing 34 community members in Mouman village. The spiders are gathered during three to four days a month before the monsoon, with each trip yielding about 20 to 30 individuals. Collected from burrows near sal trees, they are washed, fried in mustard oil and eaten whole as a seasonal delicacy passed down through generations. Rabha elders describe it as both food and rite of passage, though researchers note the study does not establish its nutritional composition or conservation status.
items.title: Rabha Community's Traditional Tarantula Harvest Documented

items.summary: Carnelian Mutual Fund raised about ₹632 crore in its maiden new fund offer through roughly 30,000 applications. An average ticket size of around ₹2.07 lakh spanned every state, with 45 per cent of applications coming from beyond the top 30 cities and units allotted on November 5, 2026.
items.title: Carnelian Mutual Fund's Maiden Small-Cap NFO Draws ₹632 Crore

items.summary: As Diwali approaches, Delhi-NCR faces hazardous air while Mumbai stays unhealthy, prompting a surge in persistent coughs across India's largest cities. Doctors explain that the symptoms of smog exposure, seasonal influenza and common colds overlap so closely that self-diagnosis is unreliable. Dr Rommel Tickoo notes the similarity makes identifying causes difficult, while Dr Sagar Srivastava points to shared signs like sore throat and breathlessness. The cough may also linger for weeks due to post-viral airway sensitivity worsened by pollution. Experts advise seeing a clinician if breathlessness, chest pain or fever appear, and recommend flu vaccination as a precaution.
items.title: Delhi and Mumbai doctors weigh pollution cough against flu

items.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that the 24-hour deadline to produce a detained person before a magistrate begins at custody, not formal arrest. A bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar held treating detention and formal arrest as separate events is constitutionally unsustainable. Petitioners alleged authorities delayed recording their arrest on September 30, 2025, after detaining them on September 29, 2025, to circumvent the deadline under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act. The court also directed magistrates to record when liberty was curtailed and release anyone held beyond 24 hours without production.
items.title: Supreme Court Sets Detention Start for 24-Hour Bail Rule

items.summary: The Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) will lengthen e-way bill numbers from 12 to 14 digits starting 1 January 2027, as electronic document volumes for goods movement keep rising. GSTN said in an advisory issued on 4 November that current numbering capacity is nearing exhaustion. Finance ministry data presented in the Lok Sabha shows bills generated climbing from 773.9 million in FY22 to 1,419 million in FY26, up nearly 83%. The change is a backend upgrade only; thresholds and compliance rules stay unchanged. Businesses must update systems ahead of the date. Pankaj Dikshit of Cygnet.One called it a necessary technology upgrade to support growth.
items.title: GSTN Extends E-Way Bill Numbers to 14 Digits From January 2027

items.summary: Rahul Matthan, in his book Ex Machina: Essays on a Decade of Tech Policy (Westland), argues that India’s privacy approach should shift from consent to accountability. He notes the country has no formal privacy statute but eight rules under the Information Technology Act, 2000 built around prior permission—a model he calls dead given today’s data volumes and technologies like big data and neural networks. Matthan contends regulators should instead focus on making organisations accountable for how they handle personal data, positioning India as able to leapfrog older frameworks. The piece draws partly on Charles Colman’s scholarship about Samuel Warren’s 1890 Right to Privacy article and its role in LGBTQ+ protections.
items.title: Lawyer Argues India Should Prioritise Data Accountability Over Consent

items.summary: BSP chief Mayawati questioned the credibility of electronic voting machines ahead of Uttar Pradesh polls, alleging they were used to influence free and fair voting. Reporting by Press Trust of India carried her claims that a large section of voters want ballot papers restored. She said concerns predate Congress-led governments and now reflect wider public demand.
items.title: Mayawati Challenges EVM Credibility, Calls for Ballot Paper Return

items.summary: The Central government told a Supreme Court bench, led by the Chief Justice of India, that it is considering appointing a committee to review the controversial UGC Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions Regulations. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said the issue was being examined so every student feels protected and no section dissatisfied. The court granted more time for guidelines on caste-based discrimination and ragging; the regulations remain stayed.
items.title: Supreme Court Grants Time on UGC Caste Rules

items.summary: Germany's MBDA Deutschland won a contract for its first airborne laser demonstrator, aiming to counter drones and cruise missiles on future Luftwaffe aircraft. India's DRDO seeks an industry partner for a 30kW-class counter-drone laser that completed trials in August 2025, following Operation Sindoor in May 2025. MBDA claims it demonstrated a full system as early as 2012. Lasers engage at light speed and run out of ammunition only when power fails.
items.title: India and Germany Invest in Airborne Laser Weapons Against Drones

items.summary: Hindustan Times reports that Delhi Police informed Municipal Corporation of Delhi officials about unauthorised construction at the three-storey Chawri Bazar building on June 15, but no action was taken. The structure collapsed Thursday morning, killing two people and injuring one. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered an inquiry, registered an FIR against the contractor, suspended two engineers, and said further investigation would reveal the cause.
items.title: Delhi Police Had Warned MCD of Unsafe Building Before Collapse

items.summary: The Centre has modified the Agnipath short-term recruitment scheme, extending a second engagement period for the remaining 75% of first-batch Agniveers who were due discharge with an Rs 11.71 lakh exit package and no pension or ex-servicemen benefits. Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani announced on October 4 that the Union Cabinet approved enrolment as regular personnel subject to selection criteria, describing it as a pathway for all Agniveers into defence forces. The Federal frames this as a course correction after four years, noting fiscal and combat-readiness concerns while flagging unresolved structural reform needs.
items.title: Modi government revises Agnipath scheme after four years of defence reforms debate

items.summary: The Union government told the Supreme Court it is contemplating a committee to revisit the University Grants Commission’s (UGC) 2026 equity regulations, which were notified on January 13 and stayed by the court on January 29. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justice Joymalya Bagchi urged the Centre to ensure the framework protects every student. The petitions mainly challenge Regulation 3(c), arguing it excludes general-category students and lacks a mechanism for false complaints, filed by Rahul Dewan, Mrityunjay Tiwari and Vineet Jindal. Upper-caste groups have protested in Delhi against the rules.
items.title: Supreme Court panel on UGC equity rules

items.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945 that would let licensing authorities immediately suspend manufacturing licences when a drug is declared Not of Standard Quality (NSQ). The draft removes show-cause delays, targets five quality parameters—assay, dissolution, related substances, impurities and sterility—and requires Root Cause Analysis before reinstatement. Licences stay open for public feedback for 30 days.
items.title: Health Ministry Proposes Immediate Suspension of Licences for Substandard Drugs

items.summary: Cummins India shares fell roughly 15% after the company reported a second-quarter net profit decline of about 19% year-on-year, with margins compressed by 680 basis points. EBITDA margin contracted to 13.9% from 21%, while domestic sales rose 5% and exports grew 2%. The firm cited disciplined execution, price realisation and cost management as it tracked external developments.
items.title: Cummins India Shares Fall After Profit and Margin Slips

items.summary: Pricol reported a 33% YoY rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 85 crore in Q2FY27, from Rs 64 crore. Revenue grew 35% to Rs 1,334 crore. Chairman Vikram Mohan cited operational efficiency and cost discipline as priorities amid changing market conditions. Shares rose around 37% over the past year.
items.title: Pricol Shares Jump After Strong Q2 Profit

items.summary: CERT-In, India's cybersecurity agency, issued an advisory identifying a hacking group it calls 'Crafty Falcon' behind AI-driven attacks on non-bank lenders, fintech firms and cryptocurrency exchanges. The agency named four tools—ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn and CyberStrikeAI—at least two of which security researchers have linked to China. CERT-In did not say who conducted the breaches or how much money was stolen.
items.title: India's CERT-In Identifies AI-Driven Hacking Group Targeting Financial Firms
